title: Universal Life Insurance Loan Risk Note: Indebtedness Surcharge on the Overloan Protection Charge
content:
The overloan protection charge on an Ashgrove Universal Life Insurance policy is raised by an indebtedness surcharge that follows the loan balance standing in the activity history as a share of the account value. The loan balance standing in the activity history is the loan advances plus the interest capitalized less the principal repaid; the account value is the one on the policy record.

## Surcharge rule

| Loan balance in the activity history as a share of the account value | Indebtedness surcharge |
|---|---|
| At or above **99%** (0.99, the high surcharge ratio) | The charge is raised by the high surcharge, **10%** (0.10) |
| At or above **97%** (0.97, the mid surcharge ratio) and below 99% | The charge is raised by the mid surcharge, **5%** (0.05) |
| Below 97% | No surcharge |

A charge raised by 10% is the charge times 1.10; raised by 5%, the charge times 1.05; the charge is rounded to the cent once, after the surcharge.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical, account value $200000.00)

| Loan balance in the activity history | Share | Surcharge |
|---|---|---|
| $198000.00 | 99% | 10% |
| $197999.00 | 98.9995% | 5% |
| $194000.00 | 97% | 5% |
| $193999.00 | 96.9995% | None |

Loan balance in the activity history: advances $185000.00, interest capitalized $12500.00, principal repaid $3000.00, giving $194500.00, which is 97.25% of $200000.00 and carries the 5% surcharge.
